85 Years On – Remembering the Siege of Tobruk – One Day Conference Melbourne and Online

Nov 9, 2026

Saturday November 14th @ 9:00 am – 5:00 pm

Tobruk House, 44 Victoria Ave, Albert Park, VIC 3206 Australia

Book Now

The troops at Tobruk are caught like rats in a trap, would live like rats and die like rats.

Nazi propagandist Lord Haw Haw, 1941
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:43
Instaread

To the thousands of Allied soldiers trapped in the Libyan coastal city of Tobruk in early 1941, this derogatory broadcast stirred a feeling of defiance deep within them, and soon the Australians christened themselves ‘The Rats of Tobruk.’

For 242 days from 10 April to 7 December 1941, these Allied forces successfully held a vital deep-water port against the German and Italian armies, thereby preventing a Nazi advance toward Egypt and the Suez Canal. The backbone of the defence was the 9th Australian Division and the 18th Brigade, as well as units from Great Britain, India, Poland and Czechoslovakia. Ships from the Royal Navy and Royal Australian Navy co-operated with aircraft from the RAF and RAAF, to keep supply routes and air defences open. Meanwhile, the Allied land forces faced concerted attacks from the German Afrika Corps and from Axis air and naval forces.

Full Program Here

2026 marks the 85th Anniversary of the Siege and with no surviving participants still alive, a new generation is taking the opportunity to re-examine the Siege at a One-Day Conference jointly sponsored by Military History and Heritage Victoria (MHHV) and the Rats of Tobruk Association. High profile speakers and subject experts will review key aspects of the Siege, and in a panel discussion seek to answer the key question of why the seemingly superior Axis forces were unsuccessful in recapturing Tobruk.

The Conference is to be staged on Saturday 14th November at the Headquarters of the Rats of Tobruk Association in Melbourne. In addition to many relics and artefacts of the Siege on show in the Hall, the venue is complemented by a Special Display created to mark the 85th Anniversary.

The conference will include presentations from Dr Robert Lyman MBE FRHS, David Mitchellhill-Green, MAJ-GEN Jeffrey Rosenfeld AC OBE, Mike Rosel, CAPT Andrew Mackinnon CSC RAN, Adam Lunney and Dr Daryl Moran along with Rats of Tobruk Descendant Guides and MAJ-GEN Jim Barry AM MBE RFD ED (Rtd)

All in person conference tickets include a Free Parking Pass, Lunch, Morning and Afternoon tea.

(Parking permit will be emailed to ticket holders 11November 2026)

MHHV Members – $75.00

NON MEMBERS – $100.00

Concession Card holders – $75.00

Online Full Day via zoom – $50.00 (Conference live link will be emailed 13th November)

Members of the RATS OF TOBRUK ASSOCIATION should register for the conference directly with the Rats of Tobruk Association Melbourne.
